title: Cohort-driven telemetry and auto-rollback playbook for batching/caching A/B
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and run an A/B experiment and associated dashboards that validate dynamic batching + prefix-KV prefetch recommendations and a fully automated safe-apply/rollback flow. Deliverables: experimental hypothesis, cohort rules, telemetry schema, dashboard panels, sequential/bayesian analysis notebook, and an automated rollback playbook integrated with CD/ops alerts.
goals: Produce automated per-customer batching/caching recommendations that reduce unit token cost without violating latency SLOs or quality thresholds
Ship a safe-config apply path with automated rollback triggers tied to signal thresholds and statistical evidence
Provide interpretable dashboards and runbook for SRE/PL to approve rollouts and audits
success_criteria: Statistically significant >=10% reduction in cost-per-1k-tokens for target cohorts (95% CI) without >8% p95 latency regression
No more than 0.5% absolute drop in model-interaction quality proxy (prompt-set pass rate) in primary cohorts
Auto-rollback triggers correctly fire in at least one injected-failure canary during testing
metrics: p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms measured end-to-end including router and runtime
tail_queue_time_ms: time waiting in batching queue
throughput_tps: tokens per second per allocated GPU pool
quality_pass_rate: fraction of curated prompt-set responses passing heuristic checks (semantic-similarity > 0.88, freshness rules)
kv_cache_hit_rate: fraction of token generations served from prefix/KV cache
fallback_rate: percent of requests routed to fallback model variant
experiment_design: Cohorts: random-geo-stratified sampling with holdout ratio 10% (control), 45% baseline config, 45% candidate dynamic microbatch+prefetch
Traffic split: deterministic bucketing by customer_id hash to ensure sticky routing across sessions
Ramp schedule: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 45% over four days; each step gated by safety signals
Analysis window: minimum 7 full days at final ramp to capture diurnal/e2e effects; primary analysis after 14 days or 200k requests per cohort (whichever first)

Statistical plan: use Bayesian sequential estimation for key metrics with ROPE for cost and latency; require posterior prob(cost_reduction >= 10%) >= 0.95 AND posterior prob(latency_regression <= 8%) >= 0.95 to call success
Power calc: assuming baseline p50 latency 110ms and target p95 220ms, we need ~80k requests/cohort for 90% power on cost reduction of 10% given observed variance
Synthetic failure injection: during canary ramp, inject 2% artificially delayed responses to verify rollback path
Counterfactual replay: rerun 48 hours of production traces through staging offline simulator to validate batching heuristics before live rollout
dashboard_widgets: Cohort Overview: live counts, traffic share, cohort allocation map
Cost vs Latency Scatter: unit_cost_per_1k_tokens vs p95_latency by customer cohort (interactive filter)
Signal Matrix: small-multiples showing p50/p95/p99 and kv_cache_hit_rate across buckets
Sequential Posterior Plot: Bayesian posterior distributions for cost reduction and latency regression updated hourly
Anomaly Watches: streaming z-score alarms for unexpected spikes in error_rate or fallback_rate
Rollback Audit Log: timestamps of auto-rollback decisions, triggering metric values, and execution trace of config revert
rollback_criteria: Immediate auto-rollback if p95_latency_ms increases by >= 12% and posterior_prob(latency_regression <= 8%) < 0.05
Auto-rollback if error_rate > 1% absolute increase over baseline sustained for 10 minutes
Auto-rollback if quality_pass_rate drops > 1.0% absolute for primary prompt-set and posterior_prob(quality_drop >= 1%) >= 0.95
Manual intervention: if kv_cache_hit_rate decreases by >20% for >30 minutes, page oncall and pause rollout for investigation
Cooldown: after any rollback, candidate config cannot be re-applied for 24 hours without explicit approval from SRE + PM
